newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says seeking $350 mln IMF loan under ESA.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says seeking $350 mln IMF loan under ESA.

text.p: Sri Lanka is seeking $350 million from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) under its Enhanced Structural Adjustment facility (ESAF), the Central Bank governor said on Friday.
"An IMF mission came last month. They have indicated that they are happy with the economic development and outlook for Sri Lanka at the moment," Amarananda Jayawardena told Reuters in an interview.
He said the team will be reporting to the IMF board next month and the ESAF programme will be decided by September.
"The ESAF is important to us because some of our economic problems cannot be changed overnight, they are long-term structural adjustments," Jayawardena said.

He said the IMF was generally happy with the way the Sri Lankan economy because the government had managed to bring the budget deficit down to 8.9 percent of groos domestic product last year against 9.3 percent in 1995. The target for 1997 is 7.3 percent.

"We are moving towards low taxes, low tariffs, (and) growth and liberalisation of the market and containing military and other expenditures. I think we have the basic ingredients for a good ESAF programme," he said.
